claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr has a low measured thermal conductivity of approximately 10–17 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.
Lattice distortion and defects such as grain boundaries and dislocations suppress electron and phonon propagation in HfNbTaTiZr.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr state is a fully random solid solution with severe local chemical lattice distortion.
Thermal annealing or related processing can induce chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr nucleates ordered B2-like HfTi and TiZr binary clusters.
A temperature range of 800–1200 K is sufficient to drive the proposed order-disorder transition while remaining below melting.
The ordered HfTi and TiZr clusters reduce local variance in atomic size and elastic constants.
Chemical short-range order flattens the local energy landscape relevant to high-frequency phonons.
The transition from random solution to ordered clusters reduces RMS lattice distortion within the cluster regions.
Reducing lattice distortion decreases phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
High-frequency phonons in the random alloy are predominantly scattered by local mass and force-constant fluctuations.
A sample-spanning network of low-distortion ordered clusters creates a continuous percolative pathway for phonon propagation.
Percolative ordering changes thermal transport from diffusive hopping to ballistic or semi-ballistic phonon propagation through ordered channels.
Percolative B2-like ordering produces a net increase in lattice thermal conductivity relative to random HfNbTaTiZr.
Ordering increases the intensity of the high-frequency phonon DOS, and this increased intensity indicates reduced phonon scattering.
Ordered cluster regions have lower mean-square atomic displacements than the random matrix.
Isolated, non-percolating ordered precipitates act primarily as scattering centers and decrease conductivity.
The proposed conductivity enhancement vanishes above the order-disorder transition temperature because B2 order is no longer stable.
Chemical or lattice-parameter disparity can hinder defect motion and contribute to hardening in other high-entropy alloys.
Interfaces between ordered clusters and the disordered matrix may add enough phonon scattering to negate the conductivity benefit.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that reduced distortion should increase conductivity only when the ordered clusters percolate. The third falsification condition instead treats reduced distortion without percolation and without a conductivity increase as falsifying the hypothesis, even though that outcome agrees with the stated boundary.
